requirement: Define reusable annotated field types that accept tags as comma strings or lists, normalize them to at most five sorted lower-case distinct values, serialize them back to a comma string, and bound and lower-case usernames.
skeleton: A before-validator splitting strings, an after-validator normalizing and capping tags, a Tags Annotated alias with a join serializer, a Username alias with length bounds and lower-casing, and a SearchQuery model using both.
caption: Reusable field types for a pydantic v2 search model, built from typing.Annotated with BeforeValidator, AfterValidator, PlainSerializer and Field metadata. Tags is a list of str annotated in order: a BeforeValidator that, only when the raw input is a string, splits it on commas, strips each part and drops blank parts, so both a b-comma string and a list validate; an AfterValidator that lower-cases, removes duplicates with a set and sorts the tags, raising ValueError saying at most 5 distinct tags when more than MAX_TAGS remain; and a PlainSerializer using str.join with commas and return_type str, so dumps turn the list back into one string. Username is a str with Field min_length=3 and max_length=20 plus an AfterValidator that lower-cases it. SearchQuery uses owner as a Username and tags and exclude as Tags defaulting to empty lists through default_factory. A ValueError from a validator surfaces as pydantic.ValidationError. The fixture asserts that Rust, python ,rust becomes python and rust with the owner lower-cased, that list input is normalized, that blank comma parts disappear, that five distinct tags pass even with a duplicate in another case while six raise ValidationError matching the message, that owners of 2 and 21 characters raise while a 3-character owner passes, and that model_dump renders tags as x,y and an empty exclude as an empty string.

plan.intent: Share field normalization rules across models
constraints: Comma strings and lists both validate as tags
Tags are lower-cased, de-duplicated and sorted
More than five distinct tags raise ValueError, surfaced as ValidationError
Usernames are 3 to 20 characters and lower-cased
Tags serialize back to a comma string

rationale.teaches: Composing BeforeValidator, AfterValidator and PlainSerializer inside Annotated aliases so normalization is declared once and reused.
rationale.why: Validation order matters: a splitter run after type validation never sees the string, and per-model validators drift apart while every single case still looks plausible.

ops.docstring: Reusable Annotated types that normalize a search query's fields.

ops.stmt:
from pydantic import (
    AfterValidator,
    BaseModel,
    BeforeValidator,
    Field,
    PlainSerializer,
)

ops.source:
Tags = Annotated[
    list[str],
    BeforeValidator(_split_csv),
    AfterValidator(_normalize_tags),
    PlainSerializer(",".join, return_type=str),
]

candidates.why_wrong: Blank comma parts survive as empty-string tags.
Tags are not lower-cased, so case variants count as distinct tags.
The cap check rejects exactly five distinct tags.
Splitting after validation never sees the raw string, which already failed as a list.
min_length=2 lets two-character owner names through validation.
